documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary group. Date of visit: 01/22/2024.
AATD PiZZ with panlobular emphysema. Completed EP chemotherapy for testicular germ cell tumor in the fall (bleomycin avoided); in complete response. Kept up weekly augmentation through treatment. Breathing at his baseline, no exacerbations. SpO2 93% RA. Office spirometry similar to 2023.
Plan: continue augmentation, tiotropium, albuterol prn. Full PFTs at next visit. Return 6 months.

documents.title: Oncology Surveillance
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside medical oncology group. Surveillance visit 02/12/2024, 4.5 months after EP x4.
Well; energy back; weight regaining. Exam: no supraclavicular nodes, left testis normal, abdomen soft.
Markers: AFP 3, hCG <2, LDH 171. No evidence of disease.
Next: markers in 3 months with CT abdomen/pelvis in May.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
26 yo, yearly exam. Feels like himself again since chemo. Weight back up to 63 kg. Breathing at baseline; weekly infusions; tiotropium daily; albuterol a few times a month. No HAE attacks this winter. Oncology surveillance clean in February. Rides a motorcycle on weekends in good weather.

Meds: alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor IV weekly, tiotropium, albuterol prn, icatibant prn. NKDA.

Exam: SpO2 94% RA. Skin: NF1 macules and freckling unchanged, no neurofibromas. Lungs diminished, long expiration. Heart RRR. Abdomen soft, no liver or spleen. L testis normal, R inguinal scar well healed. Neuro normal.

A/P:
1. AATD with emphysema: stable on augmentation. LFTs with CMP today.
2. History of testicular NSGCT: surveillance per oncology.
3. HAE: quiet.
4. NF1: BP normal, skin unchanged.
5. Screening: PHQ-9 2, GAD-7 3. Vaccines current until fall.
RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Results

documents.body: Your blood counts, kidney and liver tests are all normal. Calcium normal as well. See you in the fall for vaccines.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service: 12/07/2024 (Saturday).
CC: motorcycle crash.
HPI: 27-year-old man, unhelmeted motorcyclist, thrown from the bike and landed on his back; brought by EMS on a backboard. History of AATD with emphysema, hereditary angioedema type I, NF1, and treated testicular cancer.
Meds per patient: weekly alpha-1 infusions, tiotropium, albuterol, icatibant prn. NKDA.
Arrival vitals: BP 85/50, HR 48, RR 22, T 35.6 C, SpO2 92% on room air; breathing shallow.
Exam: GCS 15. No head or facial injury. Flaccid paralysis of both legs with absent sensation below the nipple line. Abdomen soft. Bladder distended; Foley placed, 800 mL drained.
CT spine: T4 fracture with cord injury. CT head negative.
Assessment: neurogenic shock (hypotension with bradycardia) from T4 spinal cord injury; hypoxemia with shallow breathing.
ED course: fluids, norepinephrine started, atropine for bradycardia, supplemental oxygen, blood cultures drawn, spine precautions. Neurosurgery and trauma at bedside. To ICU.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital, trauma service. Admitted 12/07/2024, discharged 12/18/2024 to inpatient rehabilitation.

Diagnoses: T4 vertebral fracture with spinal cord injury (incomplete); neurogenic shock, resolved; hypoxemia, resolved.

Course:
- ICU 12/7-12/13. Neurogenic shock managed with fluids, norepinephrine and atropine; MAP goals for cord perfusion. Blood cultures no growth; no infectious source, septic shock excluded. Pressors off 12/11. Oxygen weaned to room air 12/11.
- 12/8: posterior instrumented fusion T2-T6 with T4 decompressive laminectomy (neurosurgery). HAE: C1 inhibitor concentrate before surgery per his allergist's protocol; no swelling. No complications.
- After spinal shock resolved, exam showed preserved sacral sensation and partial motor function below T4: incomplete injury.
- Augmentation infusions held during admission, to resume in rehab.
- Foley in place at discharge, voiding trial planned in rehab.

Discharge to inpatient rehabilitation on 12/18. Meds: oxycodone-acetaminophen 5/325 as needed, tiotropium, albuterol prn, icatibant prn; augmentation to resume. Neurosurgery follow-up 6 weeks after rehab discharge.

documents.title: Mother calling - hospitalized
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt's mother called (on his HIPAA release) to let us know he was in a motorcycle crash Saturday, broke a vertebra in his upper back and hurt his spinal cord, had surgery yesterday, in ICU. Says he has a little movement in his feet today. Allergy was contacted by the hospital for his HAE before surgery. Told her we'll request records and see him after discharge. Routed to PCP.

medications.sig: 1 tablet by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain, tapered off

documents.title: Inpatient Rehabilitation Discharge Summary
documents.author: physical medicine and rehabilitation
documents.body:
Inpatient rehabilitation facility. Admitted 12/18/2024, discharged 01/31/2025.
Diagnosis: incomplete T4 spinal cord injury after T4 fracture, s/p posterior fusion T2-T6 with T4 laminectomy 12/8/2024.
Progress: steady return of lower-extremity strength and sensation. Foley removed 12/30, voiding spontaneously with low post-void residuals. Transfers independent. Walking 150 feet with a rolling walker at discharge; stairs with rail and supervision.
Weekly augmentation infusions resumed 12/26. No HAE attacks.
Pain: oxycodone-acetaminophen tapered and stopped at discharge; acetaminophen as needed.
Discharge meds: augmentation weekly, tiotropium, albuterol prn, icatibant prn.
Plan: outpatient physical therapy 2-3 times weekly; PM&R clinic in 4 months; neurosurgery 6 weeks. No driving until cleared by PM&R.

orders.reason: incomplete T4 spinal cord injury, gait training

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen with his mother, who drove. Hospital and rehab summaries reviewed.

Course: unhelmeted motorcycle crash 12/7, T4 fracture with spinal cord injury, neurogenic shock in the ICU (pressors and atropine, off by 12/11), fusion T2-T6 with T4 laminectomy 12/8 with HAE prophylaxis. Injury proved incomplete. Six weeks of inpatient rehab, home 1/31.

Now: walking indoors with a rolling walker, slow but steady. Bladder working - voiding normally since the catheter came out, no urgency or leaking. Bowels normal. Back pain 3/10, acetaminophen only, off oxycodone since discharge. Mood: frustrated, some low days, but motivated and sleeping. PHQ-9 6. Infusions back on weekly since late December. Breathing at baseline. Working from home part time.

Exam: SpO2 93% RA. Thin, 60 kg. Midline thoracic incision well healed. Hip flexors and knee extensors 4/5 bilaterally, ankles 4+/5. Light touch reduced below the nipple line but present. Gait with walker, narrow-based, no knee buckling. Lungs diminished at baseline. Calves soft.

A/P:
1. Incomplete T4 SCI s/p fusion: improving. PT referral sent to a clinic near home per rehab plan. Neurosurgery visit in March; PM&R in June. No driving until PM&R clears.
2. Neurogenic shock and hypoxemia: resolved - off list.
3. T4 fracture: healing; neurosurgery following.
4. Mood: adjustment to injury, PHQ-9 mild range; supportive talk, he declines counseling for now, will tell me if worse.
5. AATD, HAE, history of testicular cancer: unchanged; oncology aware of the admission.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Physical Therapy Evaluation
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
Outpatient physical therapy. Evaluation 02/17/2025.
Dx: incomplete T4 SCI after fusion T2-T6, home from inpatient rehab 1/31.
Findings: bilateral hip flexor and knee extensor weakness 4/5, mild proximal fatigue after 5 minutes of walking; gait with rolling walker, cadence slow. Balance: needs walker for safety in open spaces. No spasticity limiting function.
Goals: walk community distances without a device in 12 weeks; stairs reciprocal with rail.
Plan: 2-3 visits weekly for gait, balance and strengthening; home program issued. Respiratory pacing with exertion given his emphysema.

reports.text: AP and lateral thoracic spine. Posterior rods and pedicle screws from T2 to T6 with T4 laminectomy defect. Hardware intact without loosening. Alignment maintained. Healing T4 fracture.

documents.title: Neurosurgery Follow-up
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
Outside neurosurgery group. Visit 03/05/2025, 3 months after T2-T6 posterior fusion with T4 decompression.
Walking with walker indoors, cane outside. Strength improving. Incision healed. X-ray: hardware intact, alignment good, fracture healing.
Plan: continue PT, no lifting over 15 pounds for 3 more months. Recheck x-ray at 9 months.

documents.title: Oncology Surveillance
documents.author: oncology
documents.body: Outside medical oncology group. Visit 04/10/2025. Aware of his December spinal injury and rehab; recovering well. Markers: AFP 4, hCG <2, LDH 176. No evidence of disease. Next markers in 4-6 months; CT abdomen/pelvis November.

documents.title: Physical Therapy Progress Note
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
Outpatient PT, 10-week progress note (visit 04/22/2025).
Now walking household and short community distances without the walker; cane for longer outings. Stairs reciprocal with one rail. Hip flexors 4+/5, knees 5-/5. Endurance limited more by breathing than legs on hills.
Plan: continue 2x weekly for 6 more weeks, then home program.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Three months out of rehab. Walked in from the parking lot with a cane, no walker anymore. PT twice a week, graduating next month. Bladder and bowels normal. Back sore at the end of the day, acetaminophen a couple of times a week. Back to full-time work from home. Mood clearly better, PHQ-9 3.
AATD: infusions weekly, no exacerbations. HAE: no attacks this year.

Exam: SpO2 93% RA. Gait slightly wide-based with cane, steady. Hip flexors 4+/5, knee extension 5-/5. Lungs at baseline.

A/P: incomplete T4 SCI, recovering well. PM&R in June for driving question. Continue PT. Everything else stable. Physical in late summer.

documents.title: Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation Follow-up
documents.author: physical medicine and rehabilitation
documents.body:
Outside PM&R clinic. Visit 06/11/2025, about 6 months after incomplete T4 SCI.
Walking independently indoors and outdoors without a device. Mild residual weakness of both hip flexors (4+/5); remainder of lower-extremity strength 5/5. Sensation near normal below the level. Bladder and bowel continent and normal. No spasticity requiring treatment.
Driving: reaction time and lower-extremity control adequate on in-office testing; cleared to resume driving a standard car.
Plan: finish PT, keep up home program. PM&R as needed.

Plan: continue augmentation, tiotropium, albuterol prn. Full PFTs next summer. Return 6 months.

reports.text: AP and lateral thoracic spine. T2-T6 posterior instrumentation intact. Bridging bone across the instrumented levels. T4 fracture healed. Alignment unchanged.
reports.conclusion: Solid fusion T2-T6, healed T4 fracture, hardware intact.

Plan: lifting restrictions lifted. No contact sports. Follow up as needed.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27 yo, yearly exam (moved from August, his request). Walking without any device since June; PM&R cleared him to drive. Neurosurgery 8/25: fusion solid, fracture healed, restrictions lifted. Back pain rare. Bladder and bowels normal. Weight back to 63 kg. Breathing at baseline; augmentation weekly. HAE: one lip attack in the spring, icatibant x1. Oncology: no evidence of disease in April. Mood good, PHQ-9 2, GAD-7 2.

Meds: alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor IV weekly, tiotropium daily, albuterol prn, icatibant prn, acetaminophen occasionally. NKDA.

Exam: SpO2 94% RA. Skin: NF1 macules and freckling unchanged, no nodules. Thoracic scar healed. Lungs diminished, long expiration. Heart RRR. Abdomen soft. Hip flexors 4+/5, otherwise 5/5; gait normal.

A/P:
1. T4 fracture: healed - resolved on list. Incomplete T4 SCI with mild residual hip flexor weakness - stays on list.
2. AATD with emphysema: stable. LFTs today.
3. HAE, NF1: stable.
4. History of testicular cancer: surveillance.
5. Labs today incl lipids. Flu and COVID in October.
RTC 1 yr.
